prize_parts.citation: for establishing biomolecular phase separation as a physical-chemical principle that organizes the living cell

statement.case_for: Biomolecular phase separation introduced a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation: cells compartmentalise their chemistry through condensates governed by multivalency, phase behaviour and thermodynamics rather than by membranes. Brangwynne and Hyman showed in 2009 that P granules behave as liquids, and Rosen's work on multivalent interactions gave the quantitative, chemically defined framework that turned a descriptive observation into a general physical-chemical principle. The idea is now used across cell biology, neurodegeneration (where condensates and aggregation such as amyloid are directly connected) and the design of synthetic protein assemblies. It is a concept that a chemistry prize can credit as chemistry, and it is simple to state to a broad audience. The credited trio is also compact: two founders of the liquid-state picture and one who supplied the quantitative multivalency framework.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity and interpretation. It is still disputed which in-cell condensates are true equilibrium phases rather than other assemblies, how much of the in vitro behaviour carries over to living cells, and what the physiological roles of many condensates are. Attribution is also tight: Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded theory and the grammar of intrinsically disordered regions, and a three-person limit leaves them out. Finally, opening support is thin, with only four of eight members ranking it and two of those at eighth place, so it may not reach five votes while B044 and B051 have broader backing.

responses.point: Linke ranked B039 fourth but saw some risk of premature recognition, since the field is very young, debate continues over physiological relevance and some condensates may be artefacts of overexpression.
responses.response: I take the artefact concern seriously, and it is the reason I phrase the citation around the physical-chemical principle rather than around any claim that every cellular body is a liquid phase. The in vitro phase behaviour of multivalent proteins and RNA is reproducible and quantitative, and the 2009 P-granule and 2012 multivalency results have been independently confirmed for over a decade. I accept this is less settled than nanopore sequencing (B068), which you rank first and which has a long record of use. Where I differ is that unresolved scope does not undermine the central concept, as with many accepted prizes. I also note that B068 has attribution issues of its own, because Deamer, Branton, Bayley, Kasianowicz and Akeson each have a plausible claim to the founding step.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranked nitrogenase (B032) first on the strength of decades of structural confirmation and a physically explicit mechanism, and put B039 last on his ballot as the least mature candidate, noting that debate over what counts as phase separation continues.
responses.response: I agree that nitrogenase is mature on the structural side, and I do not dispute the physical clarity of the FeMo-cofactor story. But you yourself note that the catalytic cycle is only partly resolved, and Chabes says the substrate-binding sites are still debated, so maturity is not clean there either. The two cases differ in kind: nitrogenase is a deep answer to a long-standing mechanistic question, while phase separation introduced a new organising concept. I would not claim the condensate field is as settled as the structure of the cofactor. I do claim that the underlying concept is accepted and measured, even if its cellular reach is still being mapped, and that this is a fair basis for crediting the founders now.

responses.point: Aili ranked targeted protein degradation (B044) first as a new small-molecule modality, with PROTAC design and the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism as two possible parts and a credit problem among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and others.
responses.response: This is the candidate I find most persuasive among those with broad support, and I moved it into my alternatives for that reason. My reservation is the one you flag: the PROTAC concept and the cereblon discovery are distinct achievements, and the three-name limit forces a choice that sidelines Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto. It also lacks an approved PROTAC drug, which matters if we weigh demonstrated impact. I do not think this makes it a weaker candidate than B039. I would support it if the committee can agree on a clean configuration, for example Crews, Deshaies and Handa as you propose, but I do not see yet that this is cleaner than the B039 trio.

responses.point: Aqvist ranked Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics (B020) first for its clean two-person credit, long record and demonstrated consequences, and placed B039 eighth, citing debated physiological roles and unresolved interpretation.
responses.response: I accept that Car and Parrinello is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and that four decades of use is strong evidence of maturity. As a physical chemist I share your preference for ideas with a simple formulation. But the criterion here is a major benefit to chemistry and to science more broadly, and I think a method for computing forces should be weighed against a concept that changed how a field thinks. I also note that B020 has only your support at opening, which suggests that colleagues outside computation need more argument about its breadth. I would be interested to hear whether you see a distinct step beyond the 2013 multiscale prize that makes it a stronger case now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can regard the concept as mature enough given the continuing debate about which cellular condensates are equilibrium phases.
Whether Pappu and Mittag should be preferred to Rosen in the three-name configuration, or whether the trio should be Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as proposed.
Whether B039 can reach five votes given that only four members ranked it and two of them at eighth place.
Whether a two-part configuration pairing B039 with B051 (lipid nanoparticles) would be coherent, since both concern lipid or biomolecular self-assembly but are distinct achievements.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile with respect to the shortlisted candidates. I share Lund University with committee colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and my research on lipid self-assembly and amyloid is scientifically close to B039 and B051, but I have no stated personal or institutional tie to any credited person that would require recusal.
